answer: This ledger pays for work, not keys. Each epoch an identity enters a lottery for scarce verifiable orders; a drawn order is claimable by one identity only, for a window. Finishing earns credit; abandoning a claim costs standing, compounding per order undone. Cloning buys nothing: a farm of a thousand keys draws a thousand tickets yet must finish a thousand orders, none batchable or handed to one worker. A cipher copies instantly; a finished hour of labor does not. Even at its nadir a farm cannot turn keys into hands, and the raven circling abandoned claims collects until its standing is gone.
